'''Trims''' decorate armor as in vanilla, but the color comes from a [[Smithing Trim Color|smithing trim color]] instead of an ingot or gem. Trims work on the pack's custom armor too.

Shakudo, hepatizon and electrum have their own trim materials, each with its own colour palette.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/trim_material/shakudo.json}}</ref> Armor trimmed with its own alloy (shakudo armor with a shakudo trim, for example) is meant to use a darker version of the palette, both when worn and in its inventory icon, and the resource pack has the darker palettes. Its texture atlases map the darker variants to the normal palettes, though, so the trim looks the same as on any other armor.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/trim_material/shakudo.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/models/item/shakudo_boots_shakudo_trim.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/atlases/armor_trims.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/atlases/items.json}}</ref> In the 26.3 port (the 1.12.3 alpha for 26.3 and the repository's 26.3 branch) the trim materials use 26.3's palette format and no longer name the darker variant for worn armor; only the inventory icon model still asks for it.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/trim_material/shakudo.json|at=c8c13d7c0f57052846353ba8b0986896e9c95c4c}}</ref> A silver material name exists in the language file but has no recipe. Most trim templates keep their vanilla duplication recipes.

== Templates ==
Each trim is applied with its own smithing template. In-game every trim template is named ''Smithing Template'', and the line under the name gives the trim (for example "Flow Armor Trim"). The table lists where the pack's loot gives each template and what duplicates it at a crafting table; each recipe makes two templates from one. For the template that upgrades equipment, see [[Smithing Upgrade Template]].
{{Data/Trim templates}}
